question: Fresh validate profiling: total wall clock, overall parallel speedup and its true ceiling, per-step parallel speedup curves, and whether each step's thread cap is derived from those curves or guessed.
checkout: worktrees/soltiming/hermit (dedicated slot, detached, clean, commit_anchored=true, tree_dirty=false)
sha_provenance: every ledger record's own commit= field, cross-checked against git rev-parse HEAD of the checkout that ran; NOT the intended checkout
outer_jobs: CI_DAG_JOBS=16 for whole-DAG runs; CI_DAG_JOBS=1 for single-step sweeps
cache_state: warm unless a row says cold; cold = target/ debug and release both absent
driver: scripts/validate.rs (rust wrapper, safe-ci-dag-runner rust library, boxed in safe-ci.slice)
accounting: /usr/bin/time -v (RUSAGE_CHILDREN) for whole-run wall+CPU; safe-ci-dag-runner --perf-dir cgroup CSV (elapsed_s, cpu.usage_usec, effective_cores, peak_bytes) for per-step
accounting_cross_check: on the cold run /usr/bin/time reported user 2757.05s sys 780.90s wall 8:34.46 while validate.sh's own times builtin reported 45m57s / 13m01s / 8m34s -- same metric
concurrency_caveat: shared box, 15-20 other agents; between-run box load was not held constant and is recorded per row in the perf CSVs
warmups: each timed whole-DAG run followed a same-driver predecessor; the two drivers do not share a warm cargo cache
repetitions: whole-DAG configs n=1..2; replicated per-step points n=3 (marked samples=3 in results.csv); unreplicated sweep points n=1
statistic: median for n=3, single value for n=1
raw_artifacts: ignored/soltiming/ (logs, /usr/bin/time output, per-step perf CSVs, generated one-step DAG files)
